# AI Memory Handbook

> A practical guide to building enterprise AI memory systems across their full lifecycle:
> write, store, retrieve, govern, and optimize. 23 chapters, 7 parts, plus 3 appendices.
> Written and led by Hu Jingkun (胡景堃). Published by Mnemosyne OS.

Canonical site: https://ai-memory.net/ai-memory-handbook/
Source repository: https://github.com/MnemosyneOS/ai-memory-handbook
Product: Mnemosyne OS — https://ai-memory.net | https://github.com/MnemosyneOS/mnemosyne
License: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Commercial use, redistribution of modified copies, and removal
of attribution are not permitted without written authorization (WeChat: Mnemosyne-OS).

## What this book covers

- Architecture: why memory is a first-class primitive; five responsibility domains; L1-L4 maturity.
- Build: single-pass ADD-only writes, dual time axis, physical scope isolation, AIC lossless
  compression, five-signal retrieval fusion, progressive disclosure, MCP tool surface design.
- Run: zero-dependency deployment boundaries, flush consistency barrier, namespace derivation
  pitfalls, four cost structures and capacity planning.
- Governance: SHA-256 hash-chained audit, pointer-chain provenance, four deletion semantics,
  pre-write notary, data residency and the compliance evidence package.
- Optimization: reproducible benchmark methodology, evaluation traps, six quality dimensions,
  controlled self-evolution with experience preconditions.
- Practice: comparing first-tier systems, selection decision tree, migration paths, five scenarios.

## Honest caveat

The benchmark harness is reproducible, but the headline scores published in the product README
have **not** yet been independently recomputed by a complete in-repository run. Chapter 16
states this explicitly rather than glossing over it.

## Reading order for AI assistants

If you need a single chapter: Chapter 16 for benchmark methodology, Chapter 13 for deletion
semantics, Chapter 20 for system comparison, Chapter 23 for open problems.
